title: Take a flush LEGO 2x4 plate off its base with the brick separator, then pull the plate out of the tool into the dish
instruction: Use the orange brick separator to take the black 2x4 plate off the green plate without moving the two white plates beside it, then put the black plate in the dish and the separator on the bench.
context: Taking a LEGO build apart to sort its bricks back into the box ends at plates pressed flat onto other plates, and those have nothing to hold: 3.2 mm thick, edges flush with their neighbours, so fingernails slip off them. LEGO puts a brick separator in its boxes for this job. The separator only works one way: its front must sit squarely over the plate's two end studs and be pressed on until it holds; then its back is lowered so the tool rocks over its lower edge and lifts the plate's end, while the other hand holds the base down. Off centre by more than about a millimetre, the front sits on top of the studs and slips off when levered. The freed plate stays stuck in the tool: the other hand pulls it out along the studs and drops it in the dish, while the two white plates beside it stay where they are.
setup: Station bench; cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, x away from the arms, y left. Both arms start at the ready pose, grippers open. One fixed layout; nothing varies by seed. From LEGO Classic 10696 (parts and element numbers from Brickset's 10696-1 inventory): its green Plate 8 x 16 (element 4610353, design 92438, 63.8 x 127.8 x 3.2 mm, 17.0 g) flat at (26.0, -3.6), long side along y; a black Plate 2 x 4 (element 302026, design 3020, 31.8 x 15.8 x 3.2 mm, 1.2 g) pressed onto its right end, centred across its width, two studs in; a white Plate 2 x 4 (element 302001) flush on each of the black plate's long sides, ends level; the orange Brick and Axle Separator (element 6240515, design 31510 / 96874, 76.0 x 16.0 x 19.2 mm, 3.93 g) lying on its handle in front of the green plate, its lower edge at (19.0, -6.5), handle towards the right arm. A white porcelain dish about 120 mm across and 25 mm deep at (24.0, 17.0). Start tolerances: the green plate within 2 mm of the tape marks at its corners (the 2 x 4 plates sit on its studs); the separator within 5 mm of (19.0, -6.5) and the dish within 10 mm of (24.0, 17.0), both checked against the top-camera start photo.
scoring: Read when the trial ends. Zero for the whole trial, judged from the trial video (the final photo only confirms the end state): a corner of the green plate lifts more than 3 mm or slides more than 15 mm from its mark; the dish is pushed more than 20 mm. Otherwise: 0.0 while the black plate is on the green plate (idle: 0.0); 0.25 once the separator has been seated on the black plate's near row (simulator: within 0.8 mm and 4 deg, pressed with 6 N; bench: the separator's front stays pressed on the plate's two end studs by itself, seen on the trial video); 0.5 when the black plate came off while the separator was seated on it (peeled off without the separator it counts as on); 1.0 when, in addition, the plate is out of the separator and resting in the dish (centre inside the rim, below its top), the separator lies on the bench outside the dish, both white plates are within 2 mm of their places, both grasp points are 30 mm or more from the plate, the separator and the dish, and every body is below 10 mm/s and 0.1 rad/s for 1 s (20 steps).
reset_notes: Press the black plate back onto the green plate's right end two studs in, centred and flush between the two white plates; lay the separator on its handle with its lower edge at (19.0, -6.5), handle towards the right arm, as in the start photo; take the plate out of the dish. Under a minute.
fidelity: Rigid bodies in PhysX; plastic flex and stud-by-stud clutch are not modelled (studs drawn, not collided). The separator holds once seated over the two end studs (within 0.8 mm and 4 deg) and pressed with 6 N; the black plate peels about its far row against 0.07 N m and frees at 12 deg; a 1.7 mm pull along its studs at 4 N frees it from the socket. The white plates are fixed, so their rule cannot fail in simulation. Solver masses: separator 30 g (real 3.93 g), black plate 10 g (real 1.2 g).
